description: We are a team of high school students from Laos. As young, passionate individuals with a strong interest in technology and innovation, we aim to develop an educational game designed to engage young children in an enjoyable and interactive learning experience. Our project is driven by our enthusiasm for technology and our deep fascination with outer space. Through this initiative, we hope to inspire curiosity, encourage exploration, and introduce young learners to the wonders of the universe.
summary:
Project overview

This project involves the development of an educational game designed to encourage young learners who are interested in space exploration to expand their knowledge of the Solar System. The game consists of multiple missions, allowing players to select different exploration tasks. For each mission, players are provided with a specific budget to purchase the necessary rocket components and assemble their own rocket.

The primary objective is to provide an interactive learning experience in which players can develop problem-solving, decision-making, and basic resource management skills while exploring the planets within the Solar System.

The game is designed with a simple and user friendly interface to ensure that young learners can easily understand and navigate its features. Additionally, after exploring each planet, players are presented with a quiz to assess their understanding and reinforce the knowledge they have gained throughout the mission.

Overall, the project aims to combine education and entertainment by making space exploration an engaging, accessible, and interactive learning experience for young learners.
details:
Space Explorers Mission Simulator is a first-person 3D browser game where children play a space-mission engineer and astronaut. They walk through a mission-control hub, choose a destination such as Mars, Europa or Titan, and pick a launcher, spacecraft and science tools within a budget and mass limit. They place the equipment on the ship and launch. A forecast panel shows real risks, such as solar storms, engine faults and dust storms, and players can reduce them with shields, backups or insurance. After landing, they explore, collect samples and complete quizzes. They earn stars and badges that unlock new tools and worlds, and friends can join the same mission by room code. The game teaches that a mission's science goals shape its engineering choices, and that failure is a normal part of real space work. It uses real, child-friendly facts and NASA/GMAT planet textures. Its intended impact is to make space missions easy to understand and exciting for young people, to build interest in STEM, and to show that a space mission takes a whole team.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

AI tools were utilised throughout the development of this project to support game design, programming, and documentation. The following outlines their applications:

Game Design and Content Development

-Idea Generation: Used ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini to brainstorm game concepts, missions, and gameplay features.

-Educational Content: Used AI to research information about the Solar System and generate planet-related quiz questions.

-UI/UX Design: Used AI suggestions to improve the game's interface and ensure it was simple and user-friendly for young learners.

Development and Documentation

Code Generation and Assistance: Used ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini for coding assistance, debugging, and game logic development.

Documentation Support: Used AI to improve grammar, refine written content, and assist with project documentation.

All AI-generated outputs were reviewed and adapted to meet the project's requirements.
